source.title: Culinary review required before restoring Dfina and Babbouche cooking cards
source.body:
PR #29 reconciles ten dish pages with the recipe archive. Two definitions can be published, but the full cooking instructions and Recipe structured data need the following editorial decisions.

### Dfina, recipe 56

The canonical record specifies a 10-minute full stovetop simmer followed by 12–16 hours in a covered 225°F/107°C conventional oven, a check before bed or after the first three hours, and boiling water if ingredients become exposed. The existing presentation packet instead specifies 100°C for 10–12 hours without opening the pot. USDA’s general home conventional-oven guidance gives 325°F as the minimum setting. Its 140°F guidance concerns holding already-cooked food. Neither source validates the temperature history of this particular covered pot of beef, shell-on eggs and legumes.

A qualified culinary food-safety reviewer should document the tested equipment, quantities, initial cook, measured internal temperatures, transition to overnight holding and liquid checks, or approve a separately tested method. A change of oven set point alone is insufficient. Preserve the original record and its Sabbath context until the decision is recorded.

[Canonical record](https://github.com/Oak-Main/medina/blob/d8ca704bdba73b9e532b9c6ba85f7d3091f28015/lib/data/recipe-details.json) · [USDA conventional ovens](https://ask.fsis.usda.gov/article/What-is-the-lowest-temperature-you-can-set-the-oven-to-for-and-safely-cook-food) · [USDA hot holding](https://ask.fsis.usda.gov/article/At-what-temperature-should-I-hold-hot-foods)

### Babbouche, recipe 15

The archive uses food-grade live land snails, a 10-minute initial boil and skim, and a covered two-hour simmer at 190°F/88°C. It also specifies an unidentified sprig of dried wormwood and describes the broth as medicinal. The U.S. natural-flavoring standard specifies a thujone-free finished food for Artemisia. The record gives no supplier specification, species or finished-food evidence. This is a sourcing and formulation question; there is no finding that a tested sample of this broth was unsafe.

Verify a suitable food-use ingredient and preparation or approve a documented, tested botanical change. Reconcile the supplier-directed preparation language with the generic home purging instruction and remove the unsupported therapeutic description before restoring the full card. Preserve the recorded simmer and the use of food-grade snails.

[21 CFR §172.510](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-172/subpart-F/section-172.510) · [CDC guidance on edible snails](https://www.cdc.gov/angiostrongylus/prevention/)

Restore each method independently after sign-off. Check the visible ingredients, method, FAQPage and Recipe JSON-LD on the built route, then update its publication-state regression.
